items.settingsPath: Reinstall Microsoft News from the Store.
items.name: Microsoft News
items.desc: The Microsoft News app.

items.settingsPath: Reinstall MSN Weather from the Store.
items.name: MSN Weather

items.settingsPath: Reinstall the Windows Web Experience Pack from the Microsoft Store. The Widgets switch in Settings > Personalization > Taskbar comes back with it.
items.name: Widgets board and Windows Web Experience Pack
items.desc: The panel, the taskbar button, and Win+W. Uninstalls the Windows Web Experience Pack, which is the package the whole feature ships in, and the Microsoft Start app that feeds it news.

items.settingsPath: Undo the run. Spotlight itself is untouched and stays wherever it is chosen in Settings > Personalization > Lock screen.
symptoms: no fun facts on lock screen
items.name: Lock screen Spotlight ads
items.desc: Keeps the wallpapers and stops Spotlight suggesting other companies' apps and content, on every account. Spotlight's own facts and tips have no off switch while it is the lock screen; with Picture or Slideshow chosen, this turns them off too.

items.settingsPath: Settings > Privacy and security > General, and turn suggested content back on.
items.name: Settings page recommendations
items.desc: The upsell cards on the Settings home page.

items.settingsPath: Settings > Personalization > Start.
items.name: Account notifications in Start
items.desc: Removes the backup and Microsoft account prompts that appear above the power button.

items.settingsPath: Undo the run.
items.name: Finish setting up your device nag
items.desc: The full-screen prompt that appears after updates.

items.settingsPath: Settings > System > Notifications, and turn the Windows tips boxes back on.
items.name: Tips and suggestion notifications

items.settingsPath: Undo the run.
items.name: File Explorer banner ads
items.desc: Sync provider notifications, which is how Microsoft 365 and OneDrive advertise inside Explorer.

items.settingsPath: Undo the run. It is a policy, so the advertising ID switch in Settings > Privacy and security > General is locked while it is in place; afterwards it is there.
items.name: Advertising ID
items.desc: The per-user identifier used for ad personalization.

items.settingsPath: Undo the run. The policy locks the search highlights switch in Settings > Privacy and security > Search permissions while it is in place; afterwards it is there.
items.name: Search highlights
items.desc: Sponsored content in taskbar and Start search. Sets the machine-wide policy alongside the per-user setting, so a feature update cannot turn it back on.

items.settingsPath: services.msc, find Connected User Experiences and Telemetry, and set it back to Automatic.
items.name: DiagTrack service
items.desc: Connected User Experiences and Telemetry, and the WAP push message routing service that device management uses.

items.settingsPath: Undo the run. It is a policy, so Settings > Privacy and security > Diagnostics and feedback is locked while it is in place; afterwards optional diagnostic data can be turned back on there.
items.name: Diagnostic data to minimum
items.desc: Sets the lowest level the edition allows. Home and Pro cannot go as low as Enterprise.

items.settingsPath: Task Scheduler, or undo the run.
items.name: CEIP and Application Experience tasks
items.desc: The Compatibility Appraiser, the startup-app and compatibility-database tasks, Consolidator, UsbCeip, the Autochk proxy, and the disk diagnostic collector.

items.settingsPath: Settings > Privacy and security > Diagnostics and feedback, and set feedback frequency back to Automatically.
items.name: Feedback frequency to Never
items.desc: Plus the Siuf scheduled tasks.

items.settingsPath: Settings > Privacy and security > General, and turn tailored experiences back on.
items.name: Tailored experiences
items.desc: Using diagnostic data for personalized tips and ads.

items.settingsPath: Undo the run. It is a policy, so Settings > Privacy and security > Activity history is locked while it is in place; afterwards it can be turned back on there.
items.name: Activity history
items.desc: Local collection and cloud upload.

items.settingsPath: Settings > Privacy and security > Inking and typing personalization, and turn it back on.
items.name: Inking, typing, and speech data
items.desc: Stops inking, typing, and speech data being sent for personalization.
items.riskNote: Stops sending typing and inking data to Microsoft. Autocorrect and text suggestions get slightly worse over time.

items.settingsPath: Undo the run. It is a policy, so Settings > Privacy and security > Location is locked while it is in place; afterwards location services can be turned back on there.
items.name: Location services
items.desc: System-wide location services.
items.riskNote: Breaks Find My Device, automatic time zone, and anything weather-related.

items.settingsPath: Undo the run. It is a policy, so Settings > Windows Update > Advanced options > Delivery Optimization is locked while it is in place.
items.name: Delivery Optimization to LAN only
items.desc: Windows already shares update downloads only with PCs on your own network by default; this locks that in by policy, so nothing can switch it to sharing with PCs on the internet.

items.settingsPath: Undo the run: it turns the policy off and sets Windows Error Reporting Service in services.msc back to Manual.
items.name: Windows Error Reporting
items.desc: Stops Windows collecting and sending reports when an app crashes or hangs, by policy and with its service and task off. Kernel crash dumps are not affected.
items.riskNote: Some vendor support workflows read Windows Error Reporting logs when diagnosing a fault.

items.settingsPath: Reinstall Cortana from the Microsoft Store.
items.name: Cortana leftovers
items.desc: The Cortana app and the policy that keeps it off. Windows 11 24H2 removed Cortana itself, so this is only offered on earlier builds.

items.settingsPath: Undo the run. These are Edge policies, so edge://settings shows them as managed while they are in place.
items.name: Edge telemetry and commerce
items.desc: Shopping, coupons, Rewards, startup boost, background mode, and its telemetry. Edge keeps updating itself.

items.settingsPath: Undo the run. Cloud content search is a policy, so Settings > Privacy and security > Search permissions is locked while it is in place.
items.name: Search and personalization tracking
items.desc: Turns off the language-list hand-off to websites and cloud search of your Microsoft and work accounts.

items.settingsPath: Undo the run. It is a policy, so Settings > Privacy and security > Find my device is locked while it is in place; afterwards it can be turned back on there.
items.name: Find My Device location reporting
items.desc: Stops Windows periodically reporting the machine's location to your Microsoft account.
items.riskNote: If the machine is lost or stolen you will not be able to locate it from your Microsoft account. Nothing else depends on this.
